# netcup_firewall_policy (Resource)

A firewall policy in the netcup SCP account, assignable to server interfaces.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "netcup_firewall_policy" "web" {
  name        = "web"
  description = "Allow SSH and HTTPS in"

  rule {
    action            = "ACCEPT"
    protocol          = "TCP"
    direction         = "INGRESS"
    destination_ports = "22"
    sources           = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
    description       = "SSH"
  }

  rule {
    action            = "ACCEPT"
    protocol          = "TCP"
    direction         = "INGRESS"
    destination_ports = "443"
    sources           = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
    description       = "HTTPS"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Policy name.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Policy description.
- `rule` (Block List) Firewall rules, evaluated in order. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--rule))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) SCP policy id.

<a id="nestedblock--rule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rule`

Required:

- `action` (String) `ACCEPT` or `DROP`.
- `direction` (String) `INGRESS` or `EGRESS`.
- `protocol` (String) `TCP`, `UDP`, `ICMP` or `ICMPv6`.

Optional:

- `description` (String) Free-text rule description.
- `destination_ports` (String) Destination port or range.
- `destinations` (List of String) Destination CIDRs/addresses.
- `source_ports` (String) Source port or range.
- `sources` (List of String) Source CIDRs/addresses.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import format: the SCP policy id
terraform import netcup_firewall_policy.web 174780
```
